fact_text: Since Decree-Law No. 18 of 2020, an employee in Qatar no longer needs a No-Objection Certificate (NOC) from their current employer to end the contract and move to another job; they follow a notice-period notification to the Ministry of Labour instead.
evidence_quote: Cancellation of no-objection certificate (NOC); employees no longer need a permission from the employer to terminate their contracts and obtain another job within the country.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: a sponsored worker is locked to their sponsor and needs the employer's written release (NOC) to change jobs. Actually: the NOC requirement was abolished by Decree-Law No.18 of 2020 and workers can move employer without the employer's permission. Action: to change employer, file the change/notice with the Ministry of Labour rather than asking the current employer for an NOC.

entity_title: Exit permit removed for most workers
fact_text: Qatar's 2020 labour reforms removed the exit permit for most private-sector expatriate workers, so they can leave the country without their employer's permission; only a small defined ratio of senior/critical staff still requires an exit permit.
evidence_quote: the removal of exit permits. In other words, expatriate workers can leave the country as they wish

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: an expatriate always needs the employer's exit permit to leave Qatar. Actually: exit permits were removed for expatriate workers in the 2020 reforms; the law now limits the requirement to a defined ratio of senior/critical staff. Action: most relocated professionals can travel out freely, but confirm whether your role is in the small 'important personnel' category that still needs an exit permit.

fact_text: Qatar states it has abolished the sponsorship (kafala) system as part of its labour reforms to strengthen migrant workers' rights.
evidence_quote: the abolition of the sponsorship (kafala) system has been a significant step toward improving the protection of migrant workers

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: a Qatar work move still runs entirely through a kafala sponsor who controls the worker. Actually: the government describes the kafala system as abolished as part of labour reform. Action: rely on the reformed labour-mobility and exit rules rather than assuming full sponsor control; the employer remains the residence-permit sponsor but no longer controls job changes or exit.

entity_title: Medical Commission exam required for residence permit
fact_text: To obtain a Qatari residence permit, the expatriate must attend the Medical Commission for a medical examination; a fee of QR100 applies (paid by card).
evidence_quote: People who wish to obtain a residence permit in Qatar shall visit the Medical Commission with all the required documents to undergo a medical examination.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: the entry visa is enough and any medical was done back home. Actually: obtaining the residence permit requires attending Qatar's Medical Commission in person for a medical examination (QR100). Action: budget time and the QR100 fee for the Medical Commission visit as a residence-permit precondition after arrival.

entity_title: Medical result feeds the MOI residency system
fact_text: The result of the residence-permit medical examination (run by the Ministry of Public Health) is sent electronically to the Ministry of Interior's residency system, linking the health check directly to residence-permit issuance.
evidence_quote: The result of the medical examination shall be sent electronically to the residency system of the Ministry of Interior.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: the medical test is a standalone formality separate from immigration. Actually: the medical result is transmitted electronically into the MOI residency system, so a failed or pending medical directly blocks the residence permit. Action: complete the Medical Commission step promptly, as the residence permit cannot be finalised until the MOI receives the medical result.

entity_title: Health Card needed to use healthcare
fact_text: A separate Health Card (issued by Hamad Medical Corporation) is required to access healthcare services in Qatar and must be kept valid; renewal costs QR100.
evidence_quote: If you or a family member has a health card that has expired or will expire soon, you need to renew it to continue accessing healthcare services in the State of Qatar.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: the QID or residence permit alone gives access to Qatar's public healthcare. Actually: a distinct Hamad Health Card is required to access healthcare services and must be renewed to stay valid (QR100). Action: apply for and keep a valid Hamad Health Card in addition to the QID.

entity_title: Medical checkup within 30 days of entry
fact_text: An expatriate entering Qatar on a residence visa must complete the medical checkup within thirty days of entry; the fingerprint is taken after the medical examination and only then are the residency procedures completed.
evidence_quote: If an expatriate enters on a residence visa he must perform the medical checkup after entering the country within a period of thirty days.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: there is no rush on formalities after arriving on a residence visa. Actually: the MOI requires the medical checkup within thirty days of entry, followed by fingerprinting, before residency procedures can be completed. Action: schedule the Medical Commission checkup within the first 30 days after arrival to stay within the deadline.

entity_title: Qatar ID issued by MOI Expatriate Affairs
fact_text: The Ministry of Interior's Expatriates Affairs Department issues the ID number and Qatar ID (QID) card for every expatriate; the QID is the single identifier used across government and daily services.
evidence_quote: To issue ID numbers and ID cards for Expatriates as well as establishment numbers for companies.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: a passport and residence stamp are the main documents needed day to day. Actually: the MOI issues a Qatar ID (QID) with an ID number for every expatriate, and the QID is the identifier required for services from banking to healthcare. Action: treat obtaining and carrying the QID as the central identity step after the residence permit is granted.

entity_title: Employer must register the employee on Hukoomi
fact_text: Companies must register their employees on the Qatar e-Government Portal (Hukoomi) as part of the residence-permit medical process, making the residence-permit journey employer-driven.
evidence_quote: Companies must register their employees on Qatar e-Government Portal (Hukoomi).

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: the relocating employee handles their own residence-permit paperwork online. Actually: the employer/company must register the employee on the Hukoomi portal for the process to proceed. Action: confirm the employer has registered you on Hukoomi before expecting to complete the medical and residency steps.

entity_title: Personal-status documents must be attested by MOFA
fact_text: Personal-status documents such as a marriage contract or birth certificate must be authenticated (legalized) through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' Department of Consular Affairs to be valid for use inside Qatar; the fee is QR100 per document.
evidence_quote: This service aims at legalizing civil status documents to be used abroad and inside the State of Qatar.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: a home-country marriage or birth certificate can be used directly in Qatar to sponsor family. Actually: such civil/personal-status documents must be authenticated through Qatar's MOFA Consular Affairs (QR100 each) to be valid inside Qatar. Action: have marriage and birth certificates legalized and MOFA-attested before relying on them for family residence sponsorship.

entity_title: Sponsor NOC still needed for a driving licence
fact_text: Although the labour NOC to change jobs was abolished, a sponsor must still register a No Objection Certificate (NOC) through the MOI to allow a sponsored person to apply for a Qatari driving licence at the MOI Traffic Department.
evidence_quote: You can register a No Objection Certificate (NOC) to allow a sponsored person to complete license application procedures at the Traffic Department of the Ministry of Interior (MOI).

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: because the job-change NOC was abolished, no NOC is ever needed. Actually: a sponsor's NOC is still required for a sponsored person to obtain a Qatari driving licence via the MOI Traffic Department. Action: ask the employer/sponsor to register the driving-licence NOC on the MOI portal before applying for a Qatari licence.

fact_text: Qatar established a Workers' Support and Insurance Fund that protects workers' end-of-service and other entitlements, including guaranteeing their rights if the employer's establishment closes.
evidence_quote: guarantees their rights in case the establishment closes for any reason.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: if a Qatar employer goes under, the worker simply loses unpaid dues. Actually: a Workers' Support and Insurance Fund guarantees workers' rights, including if the establishment closes for any reason. Action: know that unpaid end-of-service or wages can be recovered through the Workers' Support and Insurance Fund if the employer closes.
